  • Tewa↗Language community association
    Connection & source
    Language community association

    Nambé identifies itself as one of six Tewa-speaking pueblos of the northern Rio Grande, north of Santa Fe; the account explicitly places its community history in New Mexico. Inspection: Opening geography/language paragraph under Nanbé Owingeh, with adjacent New Mexico context and Pueblo contact footer. Limits: One Tewa-speaking Pueblo supports the broad New Mexico route; Tewa is not treated as one government. Other Tewa communities, including Arizona, are outside this bounded evidence.

    Living Tewa-speaking Nambé community described in an undated Pueblo account. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Tiwa↗Language community / education location
    Connection & source
    Language community / education location

    Isleta's education page explicitly describes instruction in the Isleta Tiwa language for its members and descendants, and identifies the Pueblo's location in New Mexico. Inspection: Listen, Learn, & Pass it on! paragraphs; publisher/location statement at page foot. About Us opening geographic paragraph was also opened and read. Limits: Isleta Tiwa community scope; not all Tiwa varieties, Pueblos or governments. Undated class schedules and technology plans are not asserted as current.

    Undated public Pueblo program description inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗ · Supporting source 1 ↗

These are starting lists, not a complete census. Modern borders help you navigate; they are not Indigenous homeland boundaries. A connection may be historical or present-day and does not imply presence throughout a region. Directory names can overlap; the profiles explain their relationships.
